name: Nordic Modernism
summary: Modern architecture softened for a cold, dark climate: white plaster and brick, warm timber, daylight shaped with care and plans that bend to the site. Alvar Aalto, Arne Jacobsen and Sigurd Lewerentz made function humane.

philosophy.core_thesis: Modern architecture should serve the whole person: use natural materials, scarce daylight and a human scale to make function warm.
design_principles: Bend the plan to the site and the sun: use wings, fans and courtyards at angles of 15 to 45° and not a rigid box.
Use natural materials in honest form: brick, timber and copper beside white plaster, with a tactile detail at every touch point.
Treat daylight as scarce: tall, deep-set windows, roof lights and light-coloured surfaces that spread low sun into the room.
Keep the scale human: ceiling heights of 2.4 to 3m in the rooms, and low massing of 2 to 4 storeys.
Design the fittings with the building: door handles, lamps, chairs and stairs in bent plywood and brass.
Join inside and outside with a terrace, a garden room or a courtyard, and let the landscape come into the plan.
anti_patterns: Cold, rigid, glass-and-steel boxes without a human scale
Heavy applied ornament or historical pastiche
Large, undivided open-plan halls with no warm material
Large unshaded west-facing glazing in a low-sun climate
Synthetic, glossy finishes that hide the material
Plans that ignore site, slope, trees and orientation

massing.form: Low, articulated wings or a fan in plan, with a main block and lower service bars, set into the contour of the site.
massing.proportion: Long and low: 2 to 4 storeys, with wings 3 to 6 times longer than they are tall.
massing.roof: A flat or very low-pitched roof with deep eaves, or a gentle curved roof in copper or turf.
massing.relation_to_ground: The building steps with the slope; terraces, stone walls and planting join it to the ground.

structure.system: Reinforced concrete column frames with brick or plastered infill; timber for roofs and canopies.
structure.span_and_module: Column grids of 5 to 7.5m; ceilings of 2.4 to 3m; stair and window modules of 600mm.
structure.expression: The frame is quiet; the material of the wall and the detail of the joint carry the expression.

materials.finish: Matt and tactile: whitewashed or tinted plaster, oiled wood, hand-laid brick, patinated metal.

facade.composition: Plain plastered or brick surfaces, with window bands set to the room use and one accent of timber or tile.
facade.openings: Deep-set ribbon and corner windows sized for the sun path; the window-to-wall ratio is 25 to 40%.
facade.solid_to_void: Solid leads: 60–75% opaque, with warm material in the reveals.

light_and_space.daylight: Low sun is brought deep into the plan by light wells, roof lights and pale surfaces; lamps give a warm local light.
light_and_space.spatial_sequence: A compact, welcoming entry, then a stair or hall that turns and opens to the garden or courtyard.
light_and_space.interior_character: White walls, wood ceilings, a brick or tile feature, curved plywood furniture and warm pendant lamps.

ornament.attitude: Ornament comes from material and craft: no applied pattern, but the grain, the joint and the form of the handle.

rules.rule: Bring low sun deep into the plan with roof lights and pale surfaces.
Keep the rooms at a human height of 2.4 to 3m and the building at 2 to 4 storeys.
Arrange wings in a fan or at 15 to 45° to follow the site and the sun.
Use a few natural materials and vary the detail at each touch point.
Turn the stair and the hall to open to the garden or courtyard.

emotion.target_response: Warmth and calm: the viewer feels a modern building that is gentle, honest and made for people.

avoid_when: The brief asks for a monumental, sculptural or high-rise object.
The brief asks for strict machine-like repetition and no natural material.

modifiers.how: Drop the timber and curved plan, make the plan orthogonal, and use white plaster and a strict ribbon-window grid.

sources.title: Kenneth Frampton, Modern Architecture: A Critical History (Thames and Hudson, 1980)
